toegepas.na: soms van die kalwers vir hulself hou
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'van die kalwers hou' can be misread as the separable verb 'hou van' (to like the calves); 'vir hulself' makes 'keep some of the calves' unambiguous without changing the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'kon soms van die kalwers hou' reads first as the separable verb 'hou van' (could like the calves), so a Grade 5 reader stumbles.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'vir hulself hou' makes it plainly 'keep some of the calves' with the same people, qualifier 'soms' and meaning, and adds no fact.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'soveel' is the more standard written form than 'so baie' in this construction.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'so baie hande' is natural plain Afrikaans and deliberately echoes the lesson title 'Baie hande maak ligte werk', so 'soveel' is a lateral move that loses the echo.

vlae.blok: Werk te groot vir een gesin
vlae.teks: Die grond van 'n hele land moes met skoffels van yster losgekap word
vlae.rede: 'n hele land' can be read by a Grade 5 learner as 'a whole country' rather than 'a whole field'; the later 'op die lande' suggests a field is meant, but a clearer word would need the writer to choose what size of field is intended, so this is flagged rather than changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kon so 'n nuweling kalwers vir 'n jaar of twee leen
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kon vir 'n jaar of twee kalwers aan so 'n nuweling leen
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Leen' can mean lend or borrow; 'aan' makes it unambiguous that the community member lends to the newcomer.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original double-object 'iemand iemand iets leen' already means lend, not borrow (community member to newcomer); the reordering places 'n jaar of twee' directly before 'kalwers', which a Grade 5 reader can misread as 'one or two calves'.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Matches the past tense of the main clause and of the next sentence ('gehad het').
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Afrikaans has no sequence-of-tenses rule, so 'het gesorg dat dit goed gaan' is natural and correct; changing the tense is a lateral move.
